title: Finance & Legal: Budgeting, Forecasting, Procurement, Contracts, and Revenue Recognition Playbook
author: Elena Morales
content:
Overview

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's standard processes for annual budgeting, rolling forecasting, procurement approvals, contract lifecycle management, and revenue recognition/billing policies. It is intended for finance, legal, procurement coordinators, product and engineering managers, and budget owners. Follow the procedures below to ensure budget discipline, legal/compliance coverage, and consistent revrec and billing outcomes.

Scope

- Applies to all business units globally unless an explicit country-specific policy supersedes.
- Covers annual budget cycle, quarterly/rolling forecasts, procurement approvals, vendor onboarding, contract review, and revenue recognition/billing for hosted, dedicated, and private offerings.

Roles & Ownership

- Finance (owner): overall budgeting cadence, consolidated forecasts, capex/opex classification, revenue recognition guidance, and billing operations.
- Legal (owner): contract template maintenance, legal reviews, risk classification, and signature authority matrix.
- Procurement (owner): vendor onboarding, PO issuance, supplier due diligence, and contract renewals coordination.
- Budget Owner (product/engineering/gtm manager): responsible for requesting budget, justifying spend, and staying within approved allocations.
- CFO / Finance Leadership: final approval for high-value commitments and policy exceptions.

1) Budgeting and Forecasting

Annual Budgeting (High-level process)
1. Planning kickoff (Aug-Sep): Finance publishes FY planning templates, headcount assumptions, and key planning drivers.
2. Department submissions (Sep-Oct): Budget owners submit detailed operating plans, headcount requests, and capex proposals via the budgeting template.
3. Consolidation (Oct-Nov): Finance consolidates submissions, runs scenario analysis, and escalates material variances (>5% of function budget) to execs.
4. Executive review & approval (Nov-Dec): Leadership prioritizes investments, approves final budget to be published on Jan 1.
5. Communicate and load into FP&A systems (Dec-Jan).

Rolling Forecasting
- Cadence: Monthly 12-month rolling forecast, with deeper operational re-forecast each quarter.
- Drivers: revenue by product line (hosted API, Dedicated, Private), cost of goods sold (GPU costs, cloud egress), people costs, and one-time initiatives.
- Tolerance thresholds: any variance >10% vs. prior forecast or >$250k absolute triggers required variance memo and corrective plan.

Deliverables & Artifacts
- Budget submission template (XLSX) with revenue waterfalls and headcount headroom.
- Forecast variance report (monthly) with top 10 drivers.
- Capex request form and ROI justification template.

Decision Criteria & Prioritization
- Investments are evaluated on: strategic alignment, expected payback (months), incremental ARR impact, and capex budget availability.
- Headcount prioritization uses role criticality, time-to-hire, and projected utilization.

2) Procurement Procedures

Purchase Approval Matrix (summary)
- <$5,000: Team Lead approval (email ok).
- $5,000-$25,000: Manager + Finance approver (submit PO).
- $25,000-$250,000: Director + Procurement coordination + Finance sign-off.
- >$250,000: VP/CFO approval + Legal review + procurement-led RFP where applicable.

Procurement Steps
1. Requestor: Submit Purchase Request (PR) in the procurement tool with justification, SOW/quote, and budget code.
2. Procurement: Validate vendor, check for existing contracts, and perform standard vendor screening.
3. Finance: Confirm budget availability and appropriate GL coding.
4. Legal: Review contract if value/term/clauses exceed thresholds or include non-standard terms.
5. Procurement: Issue PO and track delivery.

Preferred Vendor & Discounts
- Maintain the Preferred Vendor list in the procurement tool. Preferred vendors have pre-negotiated Master Services Agreements (MSAs), net-30 payment terms unless otherwise noted, and standard liability/cyber clauses.

Procurement Checklist (minimum supporting docs)
- Approved PR with budget code
- Vendor quote or SOW
- Signed contract or PO
- Vendor onboarding questionnaire (KYC/supplier tax details)
- Invoice routing instructions

3) Contracts & Legal Process

Contract Lifecycle Summary
- Intake -> Risk Triage -> Legal Review & Redline -> Approval & Signature -> Archival -> Renewal/Renegotiation.

Intake & Triage
- All contract requests must be submitted via the Contract Intake Form. Include: counterparty name, scope, term, expected value, contact, and any data residency or security requirements.
- Legal assigns a risk level: Low / Medium / High. High-risk contracts include: unusual indemnities, broad data processing obligations, resale arrangements, or high revenue/strategic partnerships.

Review Guidelines
- Use Standard Redwood Templates (MSA, SOW, Data Processing Addendum, Reseller Agreement). Deviations must be flagged with justification.
- Standard non-negotiable clauses: limitation of liability (cap at fees paid in the prior 12 months), IP ownership (Redwood retains model/runtime code and model weights are subject to provider licensing), data rights (customer data remains customer property; Redwood collects telemetry for ops aggregated and anonymized).
- Service Levels & Credits: For Dedicated and Private deployments include SLOs and remedy tiers per the SLA appendix.

Signature Authority
- Delegated authority matrix is maintained by Legal and Finance. Snapshot:
  - Up to $100k: Head of Function or Director + Finance approver
  - $100k-$500k: VP level + Legal sign-off
  - >$500k: CFO approval and Exec sponsor
  - Any contract with security/regulatory obligations (e.g., SOC2 data residency) requires Director of Security review before execution.

Contract Storage & Retention
- All fully executed contracts must be uploaded to the Contract Repository (document ID + metadata) within 3 business days of signature. Contracts are retained according to the Records Retention Schedule (Finance retention: 7 years for tax and revrec evidence).

4) Revenue Recognition & Billing Policy (Summary)

Principles
- Revenue recognition follows ASC 606 principles: identify contract(s), identify performance obligations, determine transaction price, allocate price to performance obligations, and recognize revenue when (or as) performance obligations are satisfied.
- Revenue is classified by product line: Hosted API (consumption-based), Dedicated (capacity/reserved), Private (license + professional services).

Billing Models & Recognitions
- Hosted API (usage-based): Bill monthly in arrears. Recognize revenue as tokens are delivered (over time) tied to metered usage; deferred revenue recorded for prepaid credits.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): If billed monthly for reserved capacity, recognize ratably over the service month. If customers prepay for an annual commitment, recognize ratably over the commitment period.
- Private (license + services): License fees with significant standalone value are recognized upon delivery of license rights; professional services recognized based on percentage-of-completion (POC) or milestone, depending on contract terms.

Invoicing & Collections
- Standard terms: Net-30 for approved customers. Exceptions (Net-15, prepaid, or escrow) must be approved by Finance.
- Invoice issuance: Billing team generates invoices from billing system per contract terms. Credit memos require Finance + Revenue Ops sign-off.

Revenue Deferral & Journal Entries (examples)
- Prepaid hosted credits (customer prepays $10,000 for API credits):
  - On receipt: Dr Cash $10,000 / Cr Deferred Revenue $10,000
  - As usage occurs (e.g., $2,500 in month 1): Dr Deferred Revenue $2,500 / Cr Revenue $2,500
- Annual reserved contract prepaid $120,000 (12m):
  - On receipt: Dr Cash $120,000 / Cr Deferred Revenue $120,000
  - Monthly recognition: Dr Deferred Revenue $10,000 / Cr Revenue $10,000

Revenue Cutoffs & Close Controls
- Monthly close: Billing runs must include all usage up to the billing cutoff. Usage reconciliation must be completed within 5 business days of month end.
- Unbilled revenue: Record only when performance obligations are satisfied and amount can be measured reliably.

5) Controls, Auditing & Evidence

Required Controls
- Segregation of duties: procurement approvals separated from invoice approvers, system access limited by role.
- Two-factor approval for POs > $25k.
- Contract changes post-signature require a change order with approvals documented.

Audit Evidence (examples to retain)
- Approved PRs, POs, signed contracts, vendor invoices, payment evidence (bank remittance), and billing run reconciliation reports.
- Revrec schedules showing allocation of transaction price and recognition timing.

6) Exceptions, Escalations & Dispute Handling

- Policy exceptions must be requested via the Policy Exception Form and routed to Finance + Legal. Document rationale, mitigation, and who will monitor the exception.
- Billing disputes: Customer opens a ticket; Billing Ops acknowledges within 2 business days, investigates within 7 business days, and proposes resolution. Material disputes (> $50k) must be escalated to Revenue Ops Director.

7) Operational Playbooks & Checklists

Onboarding a New Vendor (quick checklist)
- Complete vendor onboarding questionnaire and W-9 or equivalent
- Verify insurance and security posture if vendor handles data
- Confirm GL mapping and payment terms
- Obtain approved contract or PO before first payment

Monthly Billing Close Checklist
- Run usage export and ingest into billing system
- Reconcile against telemetry (top 10 variance drivers)
- Generate invoices and route for sign-off
- Post journal entries for recognized revenue and deferred revenue amortization

8) Appendix: Templates & References
- Contract templates: MSA, SOW, DPA (stored in Legal template library)
- Budget template: Budget submission XLSX (link in Drive)
- Procurement PR form: procurement tool link
